framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, follow and publish a frontier AI framework, and review it at least annually.
framework.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with and clearly

transparency_report.summary: Every frontier developer must publish a transparency report when it deploys a new or substantially modified model; large developers must also publish a catastrophic-risk report updated every 180 days.
transparency_report.quote: conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report containing

incident_reporting.summary: Critical safety incidents must be reported to the Attorney General within 15 days of discovery.
incident_reporting.quote: of its frontier models to the attorney general within 15 days of discovering the critical safety

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be disclosed to an appropriate authority within 24 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: that incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law enforcement agency or public

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must each year retain an independent third party to audit compliance, and engage an independent evaluator of catastrophic risk at least every 120 days.
third_party_audit.quote: A large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an

whistleblower.summary: Frontier developers may not block or retaliate against employees who report catastrophic-risk dangers or violations; large developers need an internal reporting process with monthly updates.
whistleblower.quote: regulation, policy or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing or retaliates

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement for developers.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability.

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is one trained with more than 10^26 operations, counting fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
compute_threshold.quote: power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates, has annual gross revenues above $500,000,000.
revenue_threshold.quote: collectively has annual gross revenues greater than $500,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk means death or serious injury to at least 50 people, or at least $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident.
harm_threshold.quote: death of, or serious injury to, not less than 50 people or not less than $1,000,000,000 in damage

penalties.summary: Civil penalty up to $1,000,000 for a first violation and $3,000,000 for later ones, recovered only by the Attorney General in a civil action.
penalties.quote: $1,000,000 for a first violation and not more than $3,000,000 for subsequent violations

effective_date.summary: Chapter 93M takes effect July 1, 2027 (Sec. 355). Secs. 346-347 date the annual audit and 120-day evaluation from January 1, 2027 or 180 days after qualifying, whichever is later, which conflicts with Sec. 355.
effective_date.quote: 93M of the General Laws shall take effect on July 1, 2027.

notes: Drafted from S.3228 (the Senate-passed reprint of S.3178, the version the entry describes). First draft used the House text of H.5576 (no AI-safety language). The text is a 630,000-character omnibus; only chapter 93M (secs. 164 and 345-355) was read in full. DISCREPANCY: the entry says the thresholds are '>$500M annual AI-derived revenue or >$1B AI R&D spend', but this text defines a large frontier developer only by '$500,000,000' annual gross revenues. The effective-date sections also conflict (Sec. 355 says July 1, 2027; Secs. 346-347 say January 1, 2027 or 180 days after qualifying). Entry text should be re-checked by the author against any later amendment.
